why: Canary v1.1 introduces 5xx errors on the revenue-critical path while stable v1.0 has none. Canary: 10 5xx / 2455 reqs (0.41% overall); stable: 0 5xx / 7359 reqs. All 10 canary errors are on /checkout, where the canary error rate is 2.07% (10/483) against 0.00% (0/1455) on stable over the same window. The over-time breakdown shows canary 5xx at 1, 3, 3, 3 across the 0-30s, 30-60s, 60-90s and 90-120s windows, i.e. the failures persist for the whole test rather than being confined to the first window, so this is not a pod warm-up or cold-start artifact. Latency is a non-issue and does not argue for promotion: canary p50/p95/p99 are 28/96/105ms vs stable 32/94/104ms, and per-route p95 is identical on /browse (27 vs 27), /search (58 vs 58) and /checkout (104 vs 104). Judgement: 10 failures in 483 canary checkouts versus 0 in 1455 stable checkouts under identical traffic is well beyond plausible noise and points to a defect in v1.1's checkout handling. Judgement: promoting would expose ~100% of checkout traffic to a ~2% failure rate, meaning directly lost orders, whereas rolling back only delays the release; given a bad promote hurts customers, the asymmetry favours ROLLBACK. Recommended follow-up: capture the canary pod's logs/traces for the 10 failed /checkout requests to identify the fault before re-attempting the canary.
